info.description:
Flexera's Identity and Access Management (IAM) APIs enable automation for resources related to tenants, permissions and more. 

The API is available at the following endpoints, dependent upon the user/tenant zone:
| Zone        | Base URL    |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| NAM         | https://api.flexera.com/ |
| EU          | https://api.flexera.eu/ |
| AU          | https://api.flexera.au/ |

## Organization (Org)
Flexera One tenants are called organizations (orgs).
Orgs are provisioned and exist in one of the above zones. 
Users are also provisioned and exist in one zone, and may be granted access to any number of orgs in the same zone.

get.description: Retrieve an organization's access rules.

parameters.description:
Optional filter for returning access rules matching specific criteria. 

### Supported Filter Keys
| Filter     | Required | Valid Operators | Example                             | Description |
| ---        | ---      | ---             | ---                                 | ---         |
| subjectRef | no       | eq              | subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123'    | Return only access rules for the user with ID 123    | 
| scopeRef   | no       | eq              | scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:org:10'        | Return only access rules for org with ID 10          |
|            |          |                 | scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100' | Return only access rules for the project with ID 100 |
| roleName   | no       | eq              | roleName eq 'org_owner'               | Return only access rules for the org_owner role      |

### Filter Notes
- Filter parameters may be combined using the 'and' logical operator
- Filter is a query parameter, and must be URL-encoded, however examples provided below will be pre-URL-encoding for clarity
- The only valid organization scope to provide is the organization in which the API call is being executed
- If the filter expression does not include any scope, the default scope is the organization

### Examples
Find access rules for a specific user

	subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123'

Find access rules for a specific user in a specific project
	
	subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:::iam:user:123' and scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100'

Find access rules for a particular role
	
	roleName eq 'org_owner'

Find access rules for a specific service account, role and project

	subjectRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:service-account:456' and scopeRef eq 'ref:nam:10::iam:project:100' and roleName eq 'iam_admin'

get.description:
Index returns a collection of API events which occurred within an organization, ordered from oldest
to newest.

### Pagination

If the "filter" expression includes an end timestamp (e.g. "timestamp le {date}"), this endpoint will return a
paginated list of events which occurred before the end timestamp. After all events matching the filter have been
returned, the response will not include a "nextPage" attribute. However, if the request does not include a filter
expression or the filter expression does not set an end timestamp, then an empty page indicates that all available
events have been read. In this case, responses will continue to include a "nextPage" attribute to allow the reader
to keep their place while polling for new events.

Standard Flexera [rate limits](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/rate-limiting) apply.

### Retention

By default, API events are retained for 3 months. Events older than 3 months will not be returned by this API. To request
a longer retention policy, please contact Flexera Customer Support.

parameters.description:
An optional expression for filtering the collection of API events returned.

The following filters are supported:
| Filter     | Description                          | Allowed Operator | Behavior                                                                                                        | Example                              |
| ---        | ---                                  | ---              | ---                                                                                                             | ---                                  |
| timestamp  | Filters on the API event's timestamp | le               | Less than or equal to - returns only API events with a timestamp less than or equal to the provided value       |  timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |
|            |                                      | ge               | Greater than or equal to - returns only API events with a timestamp greater than or equal to the provided value |  timestamp ge '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |

* Operators must be lowercase

	* valid	: eq
	* invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the 'and' logical operator.

    To return API events which occurred between the two timestamps:	"timestamp ge '2019-10-21T10:20:50Z' and timestamp le '2019-10-22T10:20:50Z'"

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL-encoded:
	
		...?filter=(timestamp%20ge%20%272019-10-21T10%3A20%3A50Z%27%20and%20timestamp%20le%20%272019-10-22T10%3A20%3A50Z%27)

* When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 

		$ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/iam/v1/orgs/100/api-events \
			-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
			-G --data-urlencode "filter=(timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z')"

get.description:
Index returns a collection of events which occurred within an organization, ordered from oldest to
newest.

### Pagination

If the "filter" expression includes an end timestamp (e.g. "timestamp le {date}"), this endpoint will return a
paginated list of events which occurred before the end timestamp. After all events matching the filter have been
returned, the response will not include a "nextPage" attribute. However, if the request does not include a filter
expression or the filter expression does not set an end timestamp, then an empty page indicates that all available
events have been read. In this case, responses will continue to include a "nextPage" attribute to allow the reader
to keep their place while polling for new events.

Standard Flexera [rate limits](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/rate-limiting) apply.

### Retention

By default, events are retained for 3 months. Events older than 3 months will not be returned by this API. To request
a longer retention policy, please contact Flexera Customer Support.

parameters.description:
An optional expression for filtering the collection of events returned.

The following filters are supported:
| Filter     | Description                      | Allowed Operator | Behavior                                                                                                    | Example                              |
| ---        | ---                              | ---              | ---                                                                                                         | ---                                  |
| timestamp  | Filters on the event's timestamp | le               | Less than or equal to - returns only events with a timestamp less than or equal to the provided value       |  timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |
|            |                                  | ge               | Greater than or equal to - returns only events with a timestamp greater than or equal to the provided value |  timestamp ge '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z' |

* Operators must be lowercase

	* valid	: eq
	* invalid : EQ

* Filters can be combined using the 'and' logical operator.

    To return events which occurred between the two timestamps:	"timestamp ge '2019-10-21T10:20:50Z' and timestamp le '2019-10-22T10:20:50Z'"

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL-encoded:
	
		...?filter=(timestamp%20ge%20%272019-10-21T10%3A20%3A50Z%27%20and%20timestamp%20le%20%272019-10-22T10%3A20%3A50Z%27)

* When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows: 

		$ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/iam/v1/orgs/100/events \
			-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
			-G --data-urlencode "filter=(timestamp le '2020-10-21T10:20:50Z')"

| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |

parameters.description:
A filter to narrow the number of users to return. Supported
					 fields in the filter are [id, UserName]
The following filters are supported:
| Filter | Description | Allowed Operator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | ---| --- | --- | --- |
| id | Filters on the user's ID | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  id eq '123' |
| UserName | Filters on the user's UserName | eq | Equal - The attribute and operator values must be identical for a match. |  UserName eq 'Jon' |

* All operators are case-insensitive according to RFC 7644.

		e.g:
			valid  : eq
			valid  : EQ

* When used as a query string, the filter parameter value must be URL encoded.

		e.g: ?filter=(id%20eq%20'586859'%20)

	When using cURL, the same expression can be URL encoded as follows:

		$ curl -s {$BASE_URL}/scim/v2/orgs/{$ORG_ID}/users \
			-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
			-G --data-urlencode "filter=(id eq '586859')"
parameters.name: filter

Both the IdP in Flexera and the external identity provider must be configured with parameters from the other party.
An IdP must also have at least one domain verified to successfully authenticate users into Flexera One.

Refer to [Identity Provider Configuration](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/IDPConfig.htm) for detailed guides on configuring SSO.

Capabilities are automatically granted to newly provisioned orgs based on the customer's contract with Flexera, and may later be updated for various reasons.

tags.description:
Refresh tokens are long-lived, user-owned credentials for user access to Flexera One APIs.
Refresh tokens may only be generated in the Flexera One UI.
The credential value obtained from generation in the UI is sensitive, and must be stored securely as it will not be available again.
Refresh token Ids, used to reference specific refresh tokens in these APIs, are distinct from the sensitive credential obtained when the token is generated.
Users should securely retain their own refresh tokens; refresh tokens should never be shared, or stored in locations where they are accessible to other users.

A refresh token is used to generate short-lived access tokens; access tokens must be included in requests to Flexera One APIs for authentication.
Each refresh token belongs to the user who generates it, and can be used to access any resource in any org where the generating user has permission.

For security, refresh tokens that remain unused for one year will be automatically revoked.
The refresh token's expiresAt attribute indicates when the refresh token will be automatically revoked.
Each time the refresh token is used to generate an access token, the expiresAt attribute is updated to be one year in the future.
tags.name: Refresh Token

tags.description:
Flexera One uses a role-based authorization system, where the role(s) assigned to a principal determine the permission of the principal.
When a principal is granted a role in an organization, it grants access to specific resources in that org, but does not affect the principal's access in any other org.
The roles available in an org are determined by the capabilities granted to the org.

See [Flexera One Roles](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/flexeraroles.htm) for a complete breakdown of the roles available in Flexera One.
tags.name: Role

tags.description:
Each SAML2 identity provider may have multiple domains.
The domain(s) registered and verified determine which users may successfully authenticate through an IdP.

To verify a domain for an identity provider, first register the domain to get a verificationCode.
After the verificationCode's value is added to the domain host’s DNS records, the domain should be verified via the "verify" endpoint, which completes verification for that domain.

See [Adding a Domain](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/AddDomain.htm) and [Verifying a Domain with a TXT Record](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/VerifyDomain.htm) for more detail.
tags.name: SAML2 Domain

SAML2 identity providers (IdP) enable SAML2-based single sign-on (SSO), which allows users to authenticate to Flexera One through an external identity provider (instead of a password).
Both the IdP in Flexera and the external identity provider must be configured with parameters from the other party.
An IdP must also have at least one domain verified to successfully authenticate users into Flexera One.

Refer to [Identity Provider Configuration](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/IDPConfig.htm) for detailed guides on configuring SSO.
tags.name: SAML2 Identity Provider

tags.description:
Each SAML2 Identity Provider may have multiple signing keys.
Exactly one signing key is active at a time; the IdP's requestSigningKeyId attribute indicates the Id of the active signing key.

When the IdP's signAuthnRequests attribute is true, the active signing key is used to sign the SAML2 AuthNRequest (request sent by Flexera to the external identity provider, requesting to authenticate a user).
The signing key should be stored by the external identity provider to validate the signature included in the AuthNRequest.
Validating this signature confirms that the AuthNRequest was sent by Flexera One, and has not been modified.

Signing keys are valid for a fixed period of time, specified when they are generated.
Rotating signing keys involves generating a new signing key, updating the IdP's requestSigningKeyId to refer to the new signing key's Id, then updating the signing key stored by the external identity provider.
tags.name: SAML2 Identity Provider Signing Key

tags.description:
A service account is an account used by an application to access Flexera One APIs.
Users calling Flexera One APIs should use a refresh token; service account credentials should by used by machines/applications.

Service accounts, like users, must be assigned roles in an org to access resources within that org.
Service accounts may only be assigned roles in the org they were created in, and therefore may only access resources in that org.
tags.name: Service Account

tags.description:
Each service account client belongs to a service account, and consists of a clientId and clientSecret.
The clientSecret is a sensitive credential and must be stored securely.
Lost or compromised clients should be deleted immediately. 

Generally, only one of the service account's clients should be in use at a time.
The exception is during a no-downtime credential rotation, a new client must be generated and supplied to the running application acting as a service account, before the previous client is deleted. 

The service account client's clientId and clientSecret are used to authenticate with Flexera One's API.
After authentication, the application's permission in the Flexera One API is determined by the roles assigned to the service account.
tags.name: Service Account Client

tags.description:
An access rule grants permission to a subject, and has three components: a subject, role and scope. A subject may be granted any number of roles within a scope, and their level of permission is the union of all roles they are granted. 
### Subject
A subject is an entity to which permission is granted. 
The subject is referred to by its [ref](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/resource-references).
| Subject         | Ref Format               | Detail |
| ---             | ---                      | ---    |
| user            | ref:{zone}:::iam:user:{ID}                   | A user is an individual with access to Flexera One, who may have access to one or more organizations. |
| service account | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:service-account:{ID} | A service account is an account used by an application to interact with Flexera One APIs. It can access only the organization it exists within. |
| group           | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:group:{ID}           | A group is a collection of users. Roles granted to the group apply to all users within the group. |

### Scope
A scope is a context within which resources may exist and roles may be granted. 
A Flexera One organization is itself a scope. 
Organizations may also have one or more projects, each of which is a distinct scope.
The scope is referred to by its [ref](https://developer.flexera.com/docs/page/resource-references).
| Scope      | Ref Format                       | Detail |
| ---        | ---                              | ---    |
| org        | ref:{zone}:::iam:org:{ID}            | A role granted within the organization scope grants permission within the organization, and each of the organization's projects. | 
| project    | ref:{zone}:{orgID}::iam:project:{ID} | A role granted within a project grants permission only within that project. |

### Role
A role is a specific level of permission. Refer to the IAM Roles API or [Flexera One Roles](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/flexeraroles.htm) to understand details of each role.
tags.name: Access Rule

tags.description:
IP access control enables an administrator to add an optional layer of security to their organization, 
by defining IP ranges from which principals (users or service accounts) may access the organization.

- When no rules are defined, connections from any IP address are allowed
- When at least one rule is defined, only connections explicitly allowed by a rule are permitted

Regardless of IP access control rules, principals must still authenticate with their credentials. A principal who is
denied access to an organization based on IP access control may still access other organizations they are a part of.

tags.description:
Customers that function as managed service providers (MSPs) are granted the 'msp' capability. 
The 'msp' capability grants access to the MSP Customer APIs, which enable MSPs to create, manage and delete orgs for their customers.

The MSP's org, which has been granted the 'msp' capability is commonly referred to as the MSP "parent" org.
Customer orgs provisioned by that MSP parent org are commonly referred to as "child" orgs. 
MSP child orgs may be assigned a subset of the MSP parent org's capabilities. 
Orgs provisioned through this API are immediately available and functional.

Access to MSP customer orgs is granted by the owners attribute. 
Owners specified in that list are given administrator access (the org owner role is granted) to that child org. 

There is no permission inheritance between MSP parent and child orgs. 
Capabilities and org owners must be granted and created for each customer org, respectively.
When creating and updating customer orgs, MSPs may choose to either: 
* Grant org owner access to customers within their respective organizations
* Grant org owner access to someone internal to the MSP, who will then give limited permissions to users from the MSP's customer
tags.name: MSP Customer

The MSP's org, which has been granted the 'msp' capability is commonly referred to as the MSP "parent" org.
Customer orgs provisioned by that MSP parent org are commonly referred to as "child" orgs. 
MSP child orgs may be assigned a subset of the MSP parent org's capabilities. 
Orgs provisioned through this API are immediately available and functional.

Access to MSP customer orgs is granted by the owners attribute. 
Owners specified in that list are given administrator access (the org owner role is granted) to that child org. 

There is no permission inheritance between MSP parent and child orgs. 
Capabilities and org owners must be granted and created for each customer org, respectively.
When creating and updating customer orgs, MSPs may choose to either: 
* Grant org owner access to customers within their respective organizations
* Grant org owner access to someone internal to the MSP, who will then give limited permissions to users from the MSP's customer

V2 API Enhancements:
* Validates MSP capability hierarchy constraints (max_depth, max_width) during create and update operations
* Returns numberOfCustomers field in all responses, showing the count of direct child organizations
* Prevents deletion of organizations that have children, ensuring safe hierarchical cleanup
* Enhanced error responses with specific error codes for hierarchy violations
